source_en: Down from the ridge a few days.
Checking the lower parish records.
Dropping a manuscript at the printers.
Walked the fence looking for my dog.
Visiting the east side parish archive.
Seeking someone who won't answer my letters.
Coming to find my dog.
Saw lights from the summit. Came down.
Leaving food at the east gate again.
Taking my wife to the cinema.
Moving to the city. I hate quiet.
Signing my bestselling novel at the bookshop.
Buying a puppy. Never kept a dog.
Reading poems at the Writers' Union gala.
Starting at the radio station. I love talking.
My dog's safe at home. Buying cigarettes.
I've stopped writing. Selling my pens.
Back to my city parish of twenty years.
I had the dog with me last time. He's home tonight.
The mountain road was clear. First time in a while.
My dog ran off last week. I keep checking the fence.
I've been writing more. Words come easier when things are wrong.
If a large grey dog comes through this gate, hold him.
The manuscript is finished. I don't know what that means yet.
Thank you. This won't take long, officer.
See my dog by the east gate? Hold him.
I'll be out of your way now.
A cell is quieter than you'd think. I've known worse silence.
Give me something to write with, and I'll use the wall.
I wondered what God was thinking, making me. Now I'll know.
Every poem ends. Most just end badly.
Where are you coming from?
The parish above the north ridge. Road was clear. Dog stayed home.
The ridge. Walked the fence on the way down. My dog's still missing.
The eastern slope. Left food at the east gate again. He hasn't come.
My flat behind the bread factory. Town all my life. Mountains bore me.
My wife's house. She keeps it warm. She never minded the quiet.
The parish. The dog walked down with me. He's waiting by your gate.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
I sleep poorly. Always have. Otherwise, no.
I hear things at night. The wind, probably. I write until it stops.
Heavy hands. I write through it. The words always come anyway.
None. I sleep like a child. Nothing keeps me awake.
No complaints. I've stopped writing entirely, so I sleep well.
Nothing. I'm barely thirty. The body keeps up on the mountain.
I write when I can't sleep. Lately I can't sleep much.
Quiet suits me. I don't say that as a complaint.
The mountain has changed. Something about the way it sits now.
My dog's been gone nearly two weeks. I don't know where.
I've been leaving food outside the east gate. He hasn't come.
The words never came from me. I was only ever the hand.
